<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="46.39.50.179" /></noinclude><section begin="par75" />probably these forms are simply to be attributed to a Masoretic school, which in general marked the difference between certain forms by the use of ''é'' for ''ē'', and conversely ''ē'' for ''é''; cf. the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|52|n}}, and especially {{GHGpar|75|hh}}, also Kautzsch, ''Grammatik des Bibl.-Aram.'', § 17, 2, Rem. 1.—On the reading {{GHGheb|text=וּֽרֲאֵ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=11}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וּֽרֲאֶ֫ינָה}}, on the analogy of the reading {{GHGheb|text=מְצֵ֫אנָה}}, &c., {{GHGpar|74|h}}), see Baer’s note on the passage.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|o}}
3. The ''shortening'' of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (see above, k, and the note on hh) occasions in {{GHGterm|Qal}} the following changes:

(''a'') As a rule the first radical takes a helping {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, or, if the second radical is a guttural, a helping {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (according to {{GHGpar|28|e}}). Thus {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫גֶל}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִגְלְ}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫בֶז|translate=and he despised}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫בֶן|translate=and he built}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫שַׁע|translate=he looks}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫מַח|translate=and he destroyed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=23}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|p}}
(''b'') The ''ĭ'' of the preformative is then sometimes lengthened to ''ē'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֵ֫רֶא|translate=he sees}}. This, however, mostly happens only after the preformative {{GHGheb|text=ת}}, whilst after {{GHGheb|text=י}} the homogeneous ''ĭ'' remains, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫כֶל}} (but {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫כֶל}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫פֶן}} (but {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫פֶן}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫רֶב}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫רֶב}}); with middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=תֵּ֫תַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫כַהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=7}} (from {{GHGheb|text=כָּהָה}}). The unusual position of the tone in {{GHGheb|text=תֵּרֵ֫א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְתֵרֵ֫א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=10}} (so Baer and Ginsb.; ed. Mant. {{GHGheb|text=יִרֶ֫א}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְיִרֶ֫א}}) is best explained (except in {{GHGheb|text=יֵרֶ֫א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=33}}, before {{GHGheb|text=פ}}) on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=קוּמָ֫ה}}, &c., {{GHGpar|72|s}}, as due to the following {{GHGheb|text=א}}. But cf. also hh

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|q}}
(''c'') The helping vowel is elsewhere not used under the circumstances mentioned in {{GHGpar|28|d}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשְׁבְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=10}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּפְתְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=27}}; on the other hand, with ''ĭ'' lengthened into ''ē'' (see p) {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּשְׁתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּבְךְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּרְדְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵשְׂטְ}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=יֵ֫רֶא|translate=he sees}}, occurs parallel with {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּרְא|translate=and he saw}} (but 3rd {{GHGterm|fem.}} always {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫רֶא}}), the latter with the original {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} on account of the following {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, and identical with the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' of the ''imperf. consec. Hiphʿîl'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|r}}
(''d'') Examples of verbs ''primae gutturalis'' (§ 63), and at the same time {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, are {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַשׂ}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עַשׂ|translate=and he made}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂה}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַן|translate=and he answered}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}} (always identical with the corresponding forms in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫חַץ|translate=and he divided}}, from {{GHGheb|text=חצה}}. On some similar forms of {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} see {{GHGpar|76|d}}.—In the following cases the initial (hard) guttural does not affect the form: {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫חַר|translate=and he was wroth}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫חַן|translate=and he encamped}} (3rd plur. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִַּֽחֲנוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫חַדְּ}} (with {{GHGterm|Dageš lene}} and {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}) ''let it rejoice'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=9}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּז}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְיֵז}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּט}} ({{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} as well as {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}), &c., see {{GHGpar|76|b}}, c, f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|s}}
(''e'') The verbs {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה|translate=to be}}, and {{GHGheb|text=חָיָה|translate=to live}}, of which the shortened imperfects ought to be ''yihy'' and ''yiḥy'', change these forms to {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=יְחִי}}, the second {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} being resolved into ''î'' at the end of the word; but in {{GHGterm|pause}} ({{GHGpar|29|n}}) {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫הִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫חִי}}, with the original ''ă'' modified to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} with the tone (cf. also ''nouns'' like {{GHGheb|text=בְּכִי}} for ''bakhy''. in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫כִי}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֳנִי}} for ''‛ŏny'', &c., {{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, and {{GHGpar|93|x}}). For {{GHGheb|text=תֶּ֫שִׁי}}, however, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=18}}, since no verb {{GHGheb|text=שָׁיָה}} exists, we must read either {{GHGheb|text=תֵּשׁ}}, or better {{GHGheb|text=תִּשֶּׁה}} (Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=תשא}}), as {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׁה|translate=to forget}}.—Analogous to {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי}} from {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}}, there occurs once, from {{GHGheb|text=הָוָה|translate=to be}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּא}} for {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּ|translate=he will be}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=11|verse=3}}, but no doubt {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} is the right reading.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|t}}
The ''full'' forms (without apocope of the {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}}, cf. {{GHGpar|49|c}}) not infrequently occur after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, especially in the 1st pers. and in the later books, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶרְאֶה|translate=and I saw}}, twenty times, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=21}} in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}, but never in the Pentateuch ({{GHGheb|text=וָאֵ֫רֶא}} fifteen times, of which three are in the Pent.); also in the<section end="par75" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
